findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded as literal plaintext values in the Lambda environment variables (access_key = "AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE", secret_key = "wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY"). They persist in Terraform state and in the function configuration, are visible to any principal with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or state access, and cannot be rotated without a redeploy. Secrets should be retrieved at runtime from Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store using the execution role's permissions.
The function uses the end-of-life runtime "nodejs12.x", which no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known language and library vulnerabilities unpatched in the execution environment.

The environment variables holding the access and secret keys are configured without a kms_key_arn, so there is no enforced encryption using a customer-managed KMS key. The sensitive values are exposed in plaintext to any principal that can read the function configuration and in the Terraform state, compounding the embedded-credential issue. Note this is not a defect where a KMS key is present but misconfigured; the omission only weakens an already-comprised control.
